title: Decomposition patterns
summary: Nine reusable breakdown patterns, each with a null-honest success record, and verbs to propose a breakdown, try alternatives as separate attempts, compare them by downstream outcomes and record what worked.
boundaries: No verb in this pack enqueues children; an authorized requester does that explicitly.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: Decomposition patterns seed pack

value.lets_workers: Choose how to break work into verbs using proven shapes, try alternative breakdowns as separate attempts, and keep the shape that led to better downstream results, with every pattern carrying its own success record.

flow.when: For a goal that may need more than one verb; one attempt per alternative.
Turns one breakdown into child task previews; a person or authorized requester enqueues them.
After the children of two or more attempts finish.
Last: add the result to the pattern's success record.

value.first_rule: Prefer single-verb. Split only when parts have independent outcomes, permissions or recovery.

nouns.title: Breakdown pattern: do it in one verb
nouns.category_reason: A breakdown pattern is a reusable, low-token plan shape distilled from work that went well; applying it needs no fresh planning.

value.summary: Keep the work as one verb when one worker can hold the context, there is one outcome, and no step needs different permissions.
use_when: One outcome and one acceptance check set.
Fits one worker's context and time limit.
No step needs a different permission or reviewer.
avoid_when: Parts can fail independently and should be retried alone.
A step needs a different permission, tool or reviewer.
stop_rules: Stop when the acceptance checks pass or the time limit is reached.
value.budget_rule: The whole breakdown shares one budget; children never get a fresh allowance of their own.

use_when: One key uncertainty decides whether the approach works at all.

avoid_when: The probe would cost as much as the build.

stages.note: Time-boxed; answers one yes or no question.
Starts only if the probe's outcome is feasible.

stop_rules: If the probe answers not feasible, finish with no_change.
The build must check the probe's actual outcome, not only that it finished.
value.budget_rule: The whole breakdown shares one budget; children never get a fresh allowance of their own.
failure_modes: The probe asks the wrong question.
A dependency on a finished but failed probe lets the build start anyway.

verbs.title: Propose a breakdown
verbs.summary: Pick a pattern for a goal and propose child verbs with outcomes, order, acceptance checks, one shared budget and stop rules.
verbs.outcome: A private breakdown, or no_change when the goal fits a single verb.

slots.name: goal
slots.description: Pin of the goal or brief to break down.

alternative.description: Attempt label, such as a, b or c. Each label is a separate attempt.

pattern_hint.description: Pattern to try in this attempt, or any.

steps: Verify the pins. Check single-verb first; if the goal fits one verb, finish with no_change and say so.
Choose the pattern whose use_when best matches, or follow pattern_hint; different alternatives should try different shapes.
Give every child an outcome and acceptance checks. Children share one budget and never get their own.
Order children with after; never rely on a dependency finishing as proof that it succeeded.

acceptance.check: The breakdown validates against template.breakdown's schema.
The after graph has no cycle and every after refers to a child in the breakdown.
The number of children is at most max_children.
why_this_shape matches the chosen pattern's use_when.

notes: Instantiate this template once per alternative label to get separate attempts with separate leases and receipts.

verbs.title: Lower a breakdown into task previews
verbs.summary: Turn one breakdown into ordered child task previews that an authorized requester can enqueue; this verb enqueues nothing.
verbs.outcome: A private attempt plan with task previews and enqueued false.
steps: Verify the pin. Map each child to a verb template id where one exists in the library, or to a verb category.
Keep the breakdown's order and budget. Write task previews only.
Set enqueued to false. Enqueueing is the requester's explicit act with their own grants.

acceptance.check: The attempt plan validates against template.attempt-plan's schema.
enqueued is false and no task was created by this verb.
Every preview's after list equals its child's after list in the breakdown.

verbs.title: Compare breakdowns by downstream outcomes
verbs.summary: Compare two or three attempted breakdowns by what their children actually achieved: acceptance passed, children succeeded, time and cost.
verbs.outcome: A private comparison naming the better attempt, or no_change when they are equivalent.

slots.name: attempt_plans
slots.description: Pins of the attempt plans to compare.

slots.name: outcomes
slots.description: Pins of nouns recording the children's actual outcomes and receipts.

steps: Verify the pins. Use actual child outcomes and receipts, not the plans' promises.
Compare acceptance outcomes first, then children succeeded, then time and cost.
Report equal outcomes as equal; pick the cheaper only when cost is known.

acceptance.check: The comparison validates against template.comparison's schema.
children_succeeded matches the cited outcome nouns.
The attempts were compared on the same goal and conditions.

verbs.title: Record the outcome in the pattern's success record
verbs.summary: Add one success entry to the pattern's record as a new version, with receipts, and propose a pattern revision only when evidence supports it.
verbs.outcome: A new private version of the success record, or no_change when the use was already recorded.

slots.name: comparison
slots.description: Pin of the comparison, or of a single attempt's outcome.

slots.name: success_record
slots.description: Pin of the pattern's current success record version.

steps: Verify the pins. Write the new record version with the current version as its compare-and-set expectation.
Append one entry with receipts; failed and abandoned uses count.
Set trials and successes from the entries only; never estimate them.

acceptance.check: The new entry validates against template.success-entry's schema.
trials equals the number of entries and successes the number with outcome succeeded.
The write used the pinned version as its expected version.

notes: This verb updates an existing noun through compare-and-set, so its write is the one exception to create-only in this pack.
